old_findings.note: The ERC20Helper buffers are still built with split stores (selector in decimal) and copied by a while loop, so the token calls stay raw (args mem[_17 + 100 len 68]). The copy loop bound is now the constant 68 and its addresses are resolved, but one more split store is printed per call (see regressions).
Immutables read as 0 (calls to 0x0, new amount 0).

regressions.issue: The selector store writes a whole word at _17 + 32 and keeps the low 28 bytes, which already hold caller >> 32 from the word written at _17 + 36. The new text prints those 28 bytes as a separate store of the value they already have. A redundant line in each function, adding to the split stores of finding 1.
regressions.rule: A store whose value equals the current content of the bytes it writes (here the part of a masked word store that re-writes the preserved bytes) is a no-op: drop it and print only the changed bytes.

improvements: The copy loops of the transfer buffers have a constant bound (68) and resolved addresses (_17 + 100 instead of mem[64]). The dead padding write after the copy is dropped. The return data copy and the success decoding use _17 + 100.
notes: Diff of 68 lines (2 hunks, the transfer part of both migrate functions), read in full. Same semantics. Pack regex P2 4 lines.
summary: No semantic regression; the transfer copy loops are more resolved, but each migrate prints one more redundant split store, so the raw ERC20Helper calls (finding 1) remain.
